Ui.Script:
-- LootFrame.lua l.2's NUM_GROUP_LOOT_FRAMES, under the REFERENCE's own name. -- -- It carried the house `BENILLA_` prefix until an addon died on the bare one: -- `Bongos_RollBar/bar.lua:85` is `for i=1, NUM_GROUP_LOOT_FRAMES do` and got a nil limit. -- That is 1222's shadowed-global class again — the fifth instance — and the rule it -- settled applies to a CONSTANT an addon reads exactly as it does to a frame: our name for -- a global is as load-bearing as our name for a function. The prefix is right only where -- the reference has no counterpart; here it has one, with the same value (4) counting the -- same four frames, which already carry the reference's bare names two paragraphs down. NUM_GROUP_LOOT_FRAMES = 4
-- The bind-on-pickup confirm (ref StaticPopup.lua l.1371-1382, verbatim bar the TEXT() -- indirection this house dialect drops). Need/Greed on a BoP roll never reaches the wire -- directly: the seam diverts it to CONFIRM_LOOT_ROLL, the driver below raises this popup, -- and only OnAccept's ConfirmLootRoll re-enters past the gate (decision 0594, VERIFIED in -- the 5875 binary — the gate lives in the C RollOnLoot, not in the Lua). Keyed BARE, like -- every other StaticPopupDialogs entry: the key is the StaticPopup_Show argument, not a -- frame name. `id`/`rollType` arrive as the dialog's data/data2. -- The three strings quoted verbatim from the real 1.12 GlobalStrings.lua (patch-2.MPQ, -- Interface\FrameXML\GlobalStrings.lua l.2612/2818/465), following UiPanels.xml's -- DELETE_ITEM idiom rather than reading the globals: GlobalStrings is loaded from the -- PATCH CHAIN at runtime, so a bare global is nil under test and any format() over it -- errors — and an error here aborts the whole chunk, taking every function in this file -- with it. local LOOT_NO_DROP_TEXT = "Looting this item will bind it to you." -- LOOT_NO_DROP local OKAY_TEXT = "Okay" -- OKAY local CANCEL_TEXT = "Cancel" -- CANCEL
StaticPopupDialogs["CONFIRM_LOOT_ROLL"] = { text = LOOT_NO_DROP_TEXT, button1 = OKAY_TEXT, button2 = CANCEL_TEXT, OnAccept = function(id, rollType) ConfirmLootRoll(id, rollType) end, timeout = 0, whileDead = 1, exclusive = 1, hideOnEscape = 1 }
-- GroupLootFrame_OpenNewFrame (ref LootFrame.lua l.246-258): claim the first currently-hidden -- of the four frames for a freshly opened roll, seed its rollID/rollTime, and prime the -- Timer StatusBar's max before showing it (fields set BEFORE Show(), so OnShow below can -- already read frame.rollID). function GroupLootFrame_OpenNewFrame(rollId, rollTime) for i = 1, NUM_GROUP_LOOT_FRAMES do local frame = getglobal("GroupLootFrame" .. i) if frame and not frame:IsVisible() then frame.rollID = rollId frame.rollTime = rollTime getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "Timer"):SetMinMaxValues(0, rollTime) frame:Show() return end end -- All 4 already claimed: the reference has no overflow handling either (a 5th -- simultaneous roll simply finds no free frame) — its own ceiling, not a benilla gap. end
-- GroupLootFrame_OnShow's body (ref l.260-277): resolve the roll's display fields and paint -- the icon/name/backdrop. name/texture/quality may be nil while the item template query is -- still in flight (loot_roll.rs) — fall back to the fallback icon / blank name / common (1) -- quality rather than erroring, the same fallback shape LootFrame_Update uses for an -- in-flight loot row (LootFrame.xml). -- -- SPLIT OUT OF OnShow, unlike the reference, because it must be re-runnable: the ref's -- `GetLootRollItemInfo` reads live C state that is already populated when START_LOOT_ROLL -- fires, whereas ours reads a *pushed snapshot* that by construction does not yet contain a -- roll opening this frame (loot_roll.rs `feed_loot_rolls`, and the late item template on top -- of that). `UPDATE_LOOT_ROLL` re-enters here; the paint is idempotent. function BenillaGroupLootFrame_Paint(frame) local texture, name, count, quality, bindOnPickUp, itemId = GetLootRollItemInfo(frame.rollID) frame.itemId = itemId
if bindOnPickUp then frame:SetBackdrop({ bgFile = "Interface\\DialogFrame\\UI-DialogBox-Gold-Background", edgeFile = "Interface\\DialogFrame\\UI-DialogBox-Gold-Border", tile = true, tileSize = 32, edgeSize = 32, insets = { left = 11, right = 12, top = 12, bottom = 11 }, }) getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "Corner"):SetTexture("Interface\\DialogFrame\\UI-DialogBox-Gold-Corner") getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "Decoration"):Show() else frame:SetBackdrop({ bgFile = "Interface\\DialogFrame\\UI-DialogBox-Background", edgeFile = "Interface\\DialogFrame\\UI-DialogBox-Border", tile = true, tileSize = 32, edgeSize = 32, insets = { left = 11, right = 12, top = 12, bottom = 11 }, }) getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "Corner"):SetTexture("Interface\\DialogFrame\\UI-DialogBox-Corner") getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "Decoration"):Hide() end
getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "IconFrameIcon"):SetTexture(texture or BENILLA_FALLBACK_ICON) local nameText = getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "Name") nameText:SetText(name or "") local color = ITEM_QUALITY_COLORS[quality] or ITEM_QUALITY_COLORS[1] nameText:SetVertexColor(color.r, color.g, color.b) end
function GroupLootFrame_OnShow() local frame = this BenillaGroupLootFrame_Paint(frame) end
-- Per-instance CANCEL_LOOT_ROLL (ref l.487-489 OnLoad, l.279-285/493-495 OnEvent): each of the -- four frames registers and checks its OWN rollID, hiding only itself. UPDATE_LOOT_ROLL is -- the benilla extension alongside it (see BenillaGroupLootFrame_Paint) and takes the same -- per-instance shape: arg1 is the rollID whose display identity changed. function BenillaGroupLootFrame_OnLoad(frame) frame:RegisterEvent("CANCEL_LOOT_ROLL") frame:RegisterEvent("UPDATE_LOOT_ROLL") end
function GroupLootFrame_OnEvent() local frame = this if arg1 ~= frame.rollID then return end if event == "CANCEL_LOOT_ROLL" then frame:Hide() elseif event == "UPDATE_LOOT_ROLL" then BenillaGroupLootFrame_Paint(frame) end end
-- GroupLootFrame_OnUpdate (ref l.287-296): poll the remaining time each tick, clamped to the -- bar's own [min,max] exactly as the reference does (an out-of-range read — e.g. an unknown -- rollID's 0 — clamps to min rather than erroring). Bound to the Timer bar itself so -- `bar:IsVisible()` follows its (hidden) parent frame, matching the ref's `this:IsVisible()`. function BenillaGroupLootFrame_Timer_OnUpdate(bar) if bar:IsVisible() then local left = GetLootRollTimeLeft(bar:GetParent().rollID) local min, max = bar:GetMinMaxValues() if left < min or left > max then left = min end bar:SetValue(left) end end
-- Pass/Need/Greed (ref $parentPassButton/$parentRollButton/$parentGreedButton OnClick, -- l.374/398/425): one shared handler, rollType 0 Pass / 1 Need / 2 Greed. function BenillaGroupLootFrame_Roll_OnClick(button, rollType) RollOnLoot(button:GetParent().rollID, rollType) end
function BenillaGroupLootFrame_Roll_OnEnter(button, text) GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") GameTooltip:SetText(text) end
function BenillaGroupLootFrame_Roll_OnLeave() GameTooltip:Hide() end
-- The item icon's hover tooltip (ref $parentIconFrame OnEnter/OnLeave, l.341-349, minus the -- CursorUpdate/ResetCursor calls this engine has no counterpart for — see the header). Uses -- the LootFrame.xml row idiom (SetItemById + the benilla itemId extension) rather than the -- reference's SetLootRollItem, which doesn't exist here. function BenillaGroupLootFrame_Icon_OnEnter(button) local frame = button:GetParent() GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") local _, name, _, quality, _, itemId = GetLootRollItemInfo(frame.rollID) if itemId then GameTooltip:SetItemById(itemId, name, quality) end end
function BenillaGroupLootFrame_Icon_OnLeave() GameTooltip:Hide() end
-- The item icon's click (ref $parentIconFrame OnClick, LootFrame.xml l.353-361, re-expressed -- whole): CTRL previews the rolled item in the dressing room (decision 1060), SHIFT posts -- its link into an open chat edit box (decision 1059) — "link me that" being most of what a -- roll popup gets asked. Both read `GetLootRollItemLink(rollID)`, the binding this arc added -- (loot_roll.rs); it answers nil while the item template is still in flight, and both arms -- drop that nil — the ctrl one inside DressUpItemLink (DressUpFrame.lua l.10-16), the shift -- one inside BenillaChatEdit_InsertLink. -- -- Nothing else happens on this button, exactly as in the reference: the vote lives on the -- Pass/Need/Greed buttons and the icon is a preview/link affordance only. The ref's -- `this.hasItem = 1` OnLoad flag (l.338-340) stays dropped — it exists solely for the -- CursorUpdate/CursorOnUpdate ctrl-hover magnifier (l.344/351), which this button still does -- not wire (see the header). No RegisterForClicks either, also as in the reference: a Button -- is registered for LeftButtonUp by default (widget/kinds/mod.rs), which is the whole set -- this handler wants. function BenillaGroupLootFrame_Icon_OnClick(button) local rollId = button:GetParent().rollID if IsControlKeyDown() then DressUpItemLink(GetLootRollItemLink(rollId)) -- ref l.354-355 elseif IsShiftKeyDown() then -- ref l.356-359, through the shared helper (UIParent.xml): it carries the ref's own -- edit-box-visible guard AND our nil-link one, which this popup needs routinely — -- the frame is up the instant START_LOOT_ROLL fires, well before the item template -- answers, and until it does there is no link to post. BenillaChatEdit_InsertLink(GetLootRollItemLink(rollId)) end end

Scripts.OnEvent: if event == "START_LOOT_ROLL" then GroupLootFrame_OpenNewFrame(arg1, arg2) elseif event == "CONFIRM_LOOT_ROLL" then -- Ref UIParent.lua:517-524 verbatim, minus the central router: a Need/Greed on a -- BIND-ON-PICKUP roll sends nothing and asks first (decision 0594). arg1 = rollID, -- arg2 = rollType; both ride the dialog so OnAccept can re-enter ConfirmLootRoll. local dialog = StaticPopup_Show("CONFIRM_LOOT_ROLL") if dialog then dialog.data = arg1 dialog.data2 = arg2 end end
